Jordan: Heads-up from today's run: after the kernel-selection polish, we're seeing more fragmented host egress on tiny chat turns. p50 ~0.6ms, p90 ~1.9ms, p99 ~5.2ms for <150-token reqs. Trace + perf flame: https://redwood-internal/trace/3654339999
Tess: can you dump the flame top functions?
Jordan: quick sample:
```
  29% host_tokenizer::fast_path
  24% net::socket_writev_small
  15% proto::parse_message
  10% kvcache::lookup_and_miss
  6%  syscalls::writev
```
Notably net writev shows lots of tiny iovecs; TCP buffer fill looks low.
Ibrahim: seems like earlier kernel upswitch decision causes per-request flushes instead of waiting for the micro-coalesce window. We tightened latency for big batches but introduced more small-writes noise.
Kai: did we change any socket options? TCP_CORK/TCP_NODELAY bits?
Jordan: no socket flags changed. The selector change reduced the minibatch hold time when queue_depth>0 which exposes this behavior.
Tess: quick mitigations to try: 1) enable iov concat in the proxy (merge small iovs up to 8KB before writev), 2) opportunistic TCP_CORK on egress paths for short bursts, 3) small request holdback (1-3ms) for requests <150 tokens.
Ibrahim: I pushed a tiny proxy shim (local) that concatenates adjacent iovecs on same fd. Microbench: p99 host-side improved by ~1.4ms and syscall count down ~38% on the tiny-req workload. Patch snippet: `proxy/merge_iovs.rs` (diff pasted).
Tess: canary time? I'll add kvcache eviction counters and socket-write histogram so we can correlate.
Jordan: launching canary.
deploy-bot: Starting canary deploy cluster: canary-wrk-3 (rev a1b2c3). Perf job queued.
perf-bot: Canary complete. Results: tiny-req p99 reduced 1.3ms vs baseline; syscall rate -35%; kvcache miss-rate unchanged, but eviction wakeups slightly reduced. Full report: https://redwood-internal/perf/3654339999
Kai: solid. Follow-ups: 1) make iov-merging opt-in param, 2) add kernel-selector check: if estimated coalesce < X bytes, prefer slower kernel or delay, 3) measure tail latency for mixed workloads (not just tiny-req).
Ibrahim: also saw a subtle regression in long-sequence throughput when adding aggressive TCP_CORK toggling in the shim; need careful toggling to avoid head-of-line delays.
Tess: agree. For socket hints, let's try: only use TCP_CORK when consecutive iovecs queued within 500us and total size <8KB. Otherwise leave default.
Jordan: I'll open RFC with perf numbers + suggested config knobs: iov_merge_window_us, iov_merge_max_bytes, selector_coalesce_threshold. Will include the canary traces.
Kai: please include a cost estimate for CPU savings. Rough numbers from perf-run: ~3.5% CPU-reduction on ingress hosts under prod mix. Add that to RFC.
Tess: assigning follow-ups: Jordan (RFC + canary artifacts), Ibrahim (promote iov merge to opt-in), Kai (selector fallback heuristic), perf-bot (schedule 12h mixed workload run once PR is up).
Jordan: thanks team. TL;DR: kernel-selector tweak improved some long cases but increased tiny-write fragmentation; merging iovecs and a tiny holdback window recovered p99 and reduced syscall churn. Will document tradeoffs in RFC. :white_check_mark:
